title: When Tools Hurt LLM Reasoning: State-Dependent Belief Revision under External Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2508.15754v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Tool use is often assumed to monotonically improve reasoning, where external evidence is expected to help when relevant and be ignored when irrelevant. We show that this assumption fails in a state-dependent way. Across benchmarks with Python and Wikipedia tools, external evidence reliably helps when initial beliefs are weak, but can flip already-correct answers when those beliefs are strong. We frame this as a misallocation of revision authority, arguing that deferring to external evidence is suboptimal when internal support for the correct answer surpasses the tool's expected output quality. This predicts that harm should concentrate on high-confidence no-tool cases. We test this prediction with threshold localization, wrong-trace audits, and a same-clue intervention showing that revision framing changes the damage caused by misleading evidence. translated_title: 当工具损害LLM推理时：外部证据下的状态依赖信念修正
translated_abstract: 工具使用通常被认为能够单调地改善推理能力，即相关的外部证据应有所帮助，而无关的外部证据则应被忽略。我们证明这一假设会以状态依赖的方式失效。在结合Python和Wikipedia工具的多个基准测试中，当模型初始信念较弱时，外部证据能可靠地提供帮助；但当初始信念较强时，外部证据反而可能翻转原本已经正确的答案。我们将这一现象框定为“修正权威的错误分配”，并论证当内部对正确答案的支持程度超过工具的预期输出质量时，服从外部证据是次优选择。这一理论预测损害应集中在高置信度的无工具案例上。我们通过阈值定位、错误轨迹审计以及同一线索干预实验来检验这一预测，结果表明修正框架的方式会改变误导性证据所造成的损害。这些发现表明，在混合的无工具/工具辅助推理中，应当对何时将裁决权交给外部证据进行仲裁。
tldr: 该论文揭示了工具使用并非总能改善LLM推理——当模型初始信念较强时，引入外部证据反而可能翻转已经正确的答案，并将此归因于“修正权威的错误分配”，提出应根据内部支持的强度来仲裁是否采纳外部证据。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that tool use does not monotonically improve LLM reasoning—when initial beliefs are strong, external evidence can flip already-correct answers, framing this as a misallocation of revision authority and proposing that tool deference should be arbitrated based on the strength of internal support.
